ratings.reviewer_notes: Network-informed analysis directly seeks host-gene/pathway links between SARS-CoV-2 and thrombosis, identifying NET formation, endothelial injury, and platelet activation as plausible intermediates.

Patient, ex vivo, and infection-model experiments directly connect SARS-CoV-2-associated platelet-monocyte interactions to monocyte tissue factor expression and coagulation/inflammatory signaling; implicated host factors include F3, SELP-related signaling, and ITGAM/Mac-1.

Directly demonstrates that IL6 and IL8 increase monocyte F3/tissue-factor mRNA, protein, surface expression, and procoagulant activity, supporting one mechanistic segment, but it is not a SARS-CoV-2 study.

Review-level COVID-19 context describing host pathways connecting infection to coagulopathy, including tissue factor, platelet activation, NETosis, cytokines, complement, and loss of anticoagulant mechanisms.

Provides review-level support for endothelial injury and complement activation as intermediates between SARS-CoV-2 infection and clotting/systemic microangiopathy, but does not experimentally resolve a specific two-hop gene path.

Clinical cohort links NET-associated citrullinated histone H3 and von Willebrand factor biomarkers to thrombotic events in COVID-19, supporting NET/VWF-related host pathways but primarily as predictive associations.

Mechanistically tests SARS-CoV-2 protein effects on endothelial complement susceptibility and identifies ADAMTS9, SYAP1, and HIGD1A as regulators of CD59, providing explicit host-gene intermediates relevant to endothelial injury and thrombotic microangiopathy.

Systematic review specifically evaluates F3/tissue factor as a host mediator of COVID-19 coagulopathy and discusses upstream cytokines, PRR pathways, complement, extracellular vesicles, and thrombin signaling.
Review-level evidence supports complement activation and endothelial dysfunction as linked intermediates leading from SARS-CoV-2 infection to a procoagulant state.

Proposes specific host paths involving ACE2, inflammatory cytokines or viral-sensing TLRs, and F3/tissue factor–FVIIa coagulation activation, but the abstract presents these largely as mechanistic interpretation rather than direct testing.

Mechanistic review outlines several plausible host paths from SARS-CoV-2 to coagulopathy, including ACE2–angiotensin II signaling, F12/kallikrein-kinin activation, NETs, complement, thrombin generation, and impaired fibrinolysis.
